subject: Math
skill: Evaluating Statistical Claims Observational Studies And Experiments
prompt: The members of a town board wanted to assess the opinions of all town residents about expanding the public fitness center. The board surveyed a sample of $750$ town residents who are members of a local gym. The survey showed that the majority of those sampled were in favor of expanding the fitness center. Which of the following is true about the town board's survey?

choices.A: It shows that the majority of town residents are in favor of expanding the fitness center.
choices.B: The survey sample should have included more residents who are gym members.
choices.C: The survey sample should have consisted entirely of residents who are not gym members.
choices.D: The survey sample is biased because it is not representative of all town residents.

explanation: Choice D is correct. The town board wanted to assess the opinions of all town residents. To gather an unbiased sample, the board should have used a random sampling design to select subjects from all town residents. The given survey introduced a sampling bias because the $750$ residents surveyed were all members of a local gym. This sample is not representative of all town residents because not all town residents are gym members.
